breaking.headline: Dow closes above 50,000 for the first time as tech slides
breaking.fact: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 423 points, or 0.9%, to close at 50,018.70 — its first finish above 50,000 — while the S&P 500 slipped 0.5% to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq fell 1.5% to 23,733.54. Tech stocks gave back part of Monday's historic rally, when Nvidia's CEO reinstatement lifted the Nasdaq 6.5%, as tariff headlines and chip weakness hit the tape.

breaking.headline: Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, says he is in therapy
breaking.fact: Jensen Huang apologized to Nvidia employees at a Tuesday town hall, his first all-hands since the board reinstated him, telling staff he had let them down and is in therapy. He admitted violating the company's code of conduct and said his direct reports will now send behavior reviews to the board; he also told staff Nvidia needs no formal succession plan. Nvidia shares fell 5.9% to $155.38.

breaking.headline: Analog Devices plunges 17% despite beating earnings
breaking.fact: Analog Devices sank 17.4% to $312.95, the S&P 500's worst performer, after fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $4.06 a share on $4.37 billion in sales beat estimates but guidance for the current quarter fell short of Wall Street's hopes. The chipmaker had jumped about 9% on Monday in the Nvidia-driven rally before the sector reversed.

breaking.headline: USTR set to unveil new tariffs on 16 economies as soon as today
breaking.fact: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is set to announce new tariffs as soon as Tuesday on imports from 16 economies, including China, the European Union, Japan and Mexico, following a probe into excess industrial capacity. China's overall rate would stay at or below 20% and the EU, Japan and South Korea would face a 15% ceiling; the duties would likely take effect in January or February after a comment period.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide closed in Paris at €188.12, worth $206.24 at the ECB's Nov 24 reference rate of 1.0963, a 0.5% dollar gain on the day. The industrial-gas giant keeps grinding higher while U.S. tech gives back Monday's rally, its defensive profile doing the quiet work. With no company news in play, the dollar price from here mostly tracks the euro. The stock sits near the top of its recent range.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic slid 6.5% to $81.90 on Tuesday, closing below its $83 IPO price as the AI trade unwound after Monday's record rally. The stock has now given back its entire debut pop — it first traded at $111.50 last Thursday — with chips and memory names leading the retreat. With the listing barely a week old, the tape is still finding its level. Watch whether $83 flips from support to resistance ahead.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL inched up 0.01% to $91.61, its usual slow grind as the Treasury bill ETF accrues interest day by day. The fund keeps paying its monthly distribution — $0.30849 per share, ex Nov 2, paid Nov 5 — and the distribution yield sits at 4.04%. It is the quiet corner of the watchlist: no drama, just steady Treasury income. With a December Fed hike now priced as near-certain, short rates stay the story here.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet slipped 1.1% to $279.05 as Tuesday's tariff headlines and the AI unwind dragged tech lower after Monday's 4.7% S&P surge. The pullback is broad rather than Alphabet-specific, with the Nasdaq down 1.5% while the Dow climbed past 50,000 on defensive rotation. Google's AI and cloud story is unchanged by a day's tape. Watch whether buyers step in near breakout levels or the rally fades further.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly jumped 3.2% to $1,407.59, one of Tuesday's few big gainers, after Moody's upgraded the drugmaker to Aa2. The agency cited the massive growth potential of incretin therapies Mounjaro and Zepbound, the engine of Lilly's recent run. Healthcare led the tape as investors rotated out of chips and into defensives. The upgrade is a fresh fundamental stamp on a stock already priced for strong growth.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere inched up 0.2% to $296.01, holding near its highs while the broader market pulled back on tariff worries. Natural gas and LNG names are caught between firm energy prices — WTI crude rose about 2% today — and a risk-off tape punishing growth. Cheniere's contracted export volumes keep its cash flows steady through the noise. Watch gas prices and any fresh export headlines for the next move.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia slid 5.9% to $155.38, giving back part of Monday's 31.5% surge on Jensen Huang's reinstatement. At a Tuesday town hall, Huang apologized to staff, said he is in therapy, and admitted violating the code of conduct; he also said Nvidia needs no succession plan. Schumer's export-control accusation adds pressure. Sean's call stands: long-term hold until the probes and Dec 1 testimony shake out.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer climbed 3.9% to $28.46, riding Tuesday's defensive rotation as healthcare led the tape while tech slid. Pharma names are catching a bid with investors seeking shelter from the AI unwind and tariff headlines. The move adds to a steady recent run for a stock Sean holds for income as much as growth. Watch whether the sector rotation holds into the Thanksgiving-shortened week.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab dropped 7.4% to $45.98 as growth and space names sold off with the Nasdaq's 1.5% slide. The pullback is tape-driven rather than company-specific — no fresh Rocket Lab news today — after a strong run that left the stock sensitive to risk-off days. The company remains a core speculative holding with a busy manifest ahead. Watch whether a steadier tape turns this dip into a buying chance.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital rose 6.3% to $8.67, one of the day's strongest watchlist names as investors rotated toward yield and defensives. Mortgage REITs are catching a bid with the 10-year Treasury yield steady near 4.90% and a December hike now priced as near-certain. The move extends a solid stretch for a high-dividend holding. Watch the Fed's December meeting for the next read on the rate path.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SPCX, the leveraged Nasdaq ETF, fell 5.7% to $125.81 as the Nasdaq slid 1.5% on the AI unwind and tariff headlines. Leveraged funds magnify the tape in both directions, so a day like this cuts both ways — Monday's surge was equally outsized. The position is a trading vehicle, not a buy-and-hold, and days like today are the cost of the leverage. Watch whether tech stabilizes after Thanksgiving.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist rose 1.3% to $47.48, holding its ground while the broader market pulled back. Banks are benefiting from the defensive rotation and a steady 10-year yield near 4.90%, with regional lenders quietly outperforming growth names. Truist's dividend and steady earnings keep it a workhorse holding. Watch the Fed's December decision and any fresh tariff news for the next direction.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony fell 8.8% to $2.18, giving back part of Monday's bounce as the small-cap tape sold off. The stock fired the bottom-watch tripwire at Friday's close, and the Nov 23 rebound carried it to $2.39 before today's pullback. China's suspension of some critical-material export curbs until January keeps the supply-squeeze thesis on hold. The watch resumes at 8:18 AM CT for the next bottom signal.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy slid 4.6% to $5.57, easing after Monday's 10% surge off Friday's $5.30 low that re-armed the bottom watch. The pullback is broad — small caps and growth are selling off on tariff headlines — rather than uranium-specific. Nuclear expansion and government uranium buying remain the longer-term catalysts Sean is watching. The daily gap watch resumes at 8:18 AM CT for any 5-point-plus move.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero slipped 1.4% to $324.67 while WTI crude rose about 2% to $81.69, refiners lagging the energy rally on a risk-off day. The stock is a locked work-related holding, so the day-to-day tape matters less than the refining margin picture. Gulf Coast refining cracks stay the fundamental driver here. Watch OPEC+'s Nov 29 meeting on 2027 quotas for the next oil-price signal.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Target Retirement 2035 fund still shows its $28.51 NAV from Nov 23, unchanged until tonight's pricing — mutual funds strike NAV once a day after the close. The diversified mix of stocks and bonds smooths days like Tuesday, when the Nasdaq slid 1.5% while the Dow rose. It is the set-and-forget anchor of the watchlist, rebalancing as retirement approaches. Watch for Tuesday's NAV tomorrow.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: The S&P 500-anchored estimate puts VI5TC at $148.02, down 0.5% with Tuesday's market pullback after Monday's rally. The estimator tracks the S&P 500's move from its Nov 3 anchor, and Sean's own check put it within about 0.1% of the real price. The fund's actual holdings are index-linked, so the estimate moves tick-for-tick with the market. A steadier tape should lift the estimate back toward $149.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: Schwab's money fund still sits at its $1.00 NAV, paying a 7-day SEC yield of 3.78% as published Nov 23 by Schwab. The wind-down continues: balances over $1,000 keep moving into CDs under the November plan, so the position should keep shrinking. The inherited-IRA slice is exempt from the nudge until March. With a December Fed hike now priced as near-certain, money-fund yields may edge up rather than down.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Treasury money fund holds its $1.00 NAV with a 7-day SEC yield of 4.03%, published Nov 23 by Vanguard. It remains the top-yielding cash on the watchlist and the parking spot for the ANT proceeds and the Seiver Slough and Lodge sale streams in the income model. The fund owns only Treasuries, so it carries no credit risk. A December Fed hike would likely lift its yield further.

weekInBrief.headline: Fed's Williams signals a December rate hike as inflation stays high
weekInBrief.body: New York Fed President John Williams said Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point the central bank toward tighter policy, saying there is “still work to do” to return inflation to 2%. He expects inflation to end the year at 3.5% and reach target in 2028. Markets fully price a quarter-point hike at the Fed's Dec. 8–9 meeting, with some officials openly weighing a half-point move.

weekInBrief.headline: Thanksgiving travel set for busiest skies in 16 years
weekInBrief.body: The FAA forecasts more than 417,000 flights over the nine-day Thanksgiving travel period, the busiest holiday skies in 16 years, with today — Tuesday, Nov. 24 — the single busiest day at about 52,000 scheduled flights. The agency also warned of developing storms on the West Coast, in Florida and the Gulf Coast, and across the Southeast that could disrupt flights.

weekInBrief.headline: Xiamen Airlines orders 50 Boeing jets in China's biggest buy in years
weekInBrief.body: Xiamen Airlines, a unit of China Southern Airlines, agreed Tuesday to buy 50 Boeing 737-8 aircraft at a list price of about $7.4 billion, the first major Chinese purchase from Boeing in years. Deliveries run from 2031 to 2034, and the deal still needs shareholder and Chinese government approval. The order follows President Trump's statement Monday that he expects China to buy 250 more Boeing jets.

weekInBrief.headline: Richmond Fed factory gauge turns positive in November
weekInBrief.body: The Richmond Fed's manufacturing index rose to +3 in November from -2 in October, beating expectations of another contraction, with new orders swinging to +2 from -8 and employment improving to +6 from +3. The outlook firmed too, with expected shipments jumping to +28. On the less positive side, prices paid accelerated, up 7.59% over the past year.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iran's navy said Tuesday morning that two oil tankers struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, the latest in a string of attacks on commercial shipping that has hit more than 25 tankers in the past week, according to Iranian state media. Tehran's foreign ministry spokesman said Monday that Iran would use “all available means” to confront the U.S. naval blockade, which has largely halted Iranian exports since it was restored in July. Iranian fresh crude exports are near zero — Kpler puts 40 to 50 million barrels of Iranian oil still on the water in Asia, discharging in China at close to 1 million barrels a day — while non-Iranian Gulf oil keeps flowing, with flows through the strait recovered to roughly 70% of pre-war volumes, per Kpler and Goldman Sachs.

space.headline: NASA names Artemis III crew for 2027 Earth-orbit test flight
space.body: NASA on Tuesday named the four astronauts for Artemis III: commander Randy Bresnik, ESA pilot Luca Parmitano, and mission specialists Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio, with Bob Hines as backup. The 2027 mission will fly Orion into low Earth orbit to rendezvous and dock with test versions of SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon landers — the first crewed tryout of both lunar landers — before the first crewed Moon landing moves to Artemis IV in 2028.

space.headline: Vaporized rock reveals titanium oxide around a massive young star
space.body: Astronomers have detected titanium oxide in gas form around a massive young star for the first time, using ALMA to observe the disk of Orion Source I, behind the Orion Nebula. The finding marks the first region where scientists could determine the makeup of solid planet-building material beyond our solar system without collecting a sample — the vaporized rock traces the dust that seeds new worlds.

space.headline: The human ear may work very differently than we thought
space.body: New research in Science Advances challenges the long-standing model of how the inner ear detects sound: low-frequency sounds produce nearly simultaneous vibrations across widely separated regions of the cochlea, rather than peaking at one spot. Observed in guinea pigs with optical coherence tomography, the finding could lead to cochlear implants that better reproduce the ear's complex vibration patterns for people with hearing loss.

space.headline: Ancient cellular machinery boosts immunity against cancer
space.body: Cornell researchers have found a new way to rally the immune system against cancer, using ancient virus-derived machinery to produce tiny vesicles that carry antigen information across long distances to immune cells. The vesicles, made by dendritic cells, activated T cells in lab tests, and the team says the approach could strengthen cancer vaccines. The work was published in Nature Nanotechnology.

apod.title: Eruption Extends Iwo Jima's Beach
apod.credit: NASA Earth Observatory / Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey
apod.explanation: A submarine volcano off Iwo Jima's southeast shore has built about 50 hectares (125 acres) of new black-sand beach — roughly 90 football fields — enlarging the island by about 1.7%. Landsat 9 caught the coast quiet on Oct. 26, then on Nov. 11 the new land, its heat glowing orange in shortwave infrared, a gray plume drifting southeast, and a streak of floating pumice. Japan's Coast Guard confirmed the new land Nov. 16; scientists expect waves to wash it away within a few months, as happened after the 2023 eruption.
